thread:
lina: heads-up — nightly perf dashboard threw a regression on gpt-edge-quant path, 95p latency +22% vs baseline :alarm_clock:
rahul: saw that, digging. is this only on dedicated hosts or hosted too?
marta: dedicated only from the quick look, canary graphs show the spike around 02:10 UTC.
perf-bot: [perf-alert] metric=latency_95 model=gpt-edge-quant cluster=prod-dedicated delta=22% baseline=48ms now=58.6ms link=https://dash.re/redwood/perf/alerts/1769001234
sri: timeline — any recent merges touching kernel selection or batching heuristics?
lina: yes, merged PR #1247 yesterday: kernel-selector now prefers nv-fused-attn for matmul sizes > 4096 and switches batching window policy to adaptive-early-exit.
rahul: that PR also changed KV cache lookup ordering (move L1 before L2) to reduce mem traffic. could be interaction.
marta: quick profiler from the canary at 02:15 (short run):
```
CPU: user 12% sys 6%
GPU kernels: nv-fused-attn 48% (avg 1.8ms/op), generic-attn 30% (avg 1.2ms/op)
KV hit-rate: prefix_cache 69% (baseline ~93%)
batch sizes: mean=3.1 (baseline 2.8)
latency p95=59ms (baseline 48ms)
```
rahul: interesting — nv-fused-attn has higher per-op time here, maybe due to seq-len distribution we have on prod. selector decision might be flipping to a slower kernel for typical traces.
sri: can we reproduce with a local micro-bench? run model traces from prod sample with the new kernel selector on a dedicated instance and measure per-kernel times.
lina: running now against trace shard s-2026-03-17-22: start 1769001300
perf-bot: CI perf check: nightly-ci/job-serve-perf failed — p95 increased 18% on macos-runner-3; logs: https://ci.re/redwood/1769001300/logs
marta: bisect candidate list: PRs touching kernel selector and batching (1239, 1247, 1251). 1247 looks highest risk.
rahul: I tried a quick local revert of the kernel-selector change — p95 drops back to baseline in the same trace. provisional revert helps.
sri: great — hold rollout for that change. can we patch selector with an immediate heuristic: if seq_len_mean < 1024 prefer generic-attn override?
lina: I pushed a hotfix branch (hotfix/selector-fallback) that forces generic-attn for seq_len_mean<2048 and disabled adaptive-early-exit batching. requesting an expedited canary.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started for hotfix/selector-fallback to prod-dedicated-canary at 1769001450.
perf-bot: canary results (5m): p95 reverted to +2% vs baseline, prefix_cache hit-rate returned to 92%, nv-fused-attn usage dropped to 12%.
marta: KV cache hit drop earlier is worrying — maybe the L1-before-L2 reorder caused some eviction pattern with the new batching. note for postmortem.
rahul: will open revert PR for #1247 and include the hotfix as interim. PR draft: revert-1247-kernel-selector — tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml.
sri: also add a CI perf test that runs the sampled trace and asserts p95 < baseline * 1.05 to catch this before merge.
lina: agreed. adding regression test to nightly-ci and adding a small unit test for kernel selector thresholds.
marta: thanks all — leaving rollout hold until revert lands and CI passes. will track follow-up items: KV eviction behavior, batching heuristic regression, and selector unit tests. :white_check_mark:
rahul: follow-up: I'll attach the full flamegraph and kernel timing diffs to the PR for postmortem context.
lina: closing the alert thread now but keeping pinned notes in the PR. good catch, perf-bot.
perf-bot: alert resolved at 1769001598.
